messages:
Jamie: Hey team — quick ask. We're chasing a customer-reported failure in /v1/infer/batch that only reproduces with real prompt payloads. Can we temporarily capture full request bodies (headers + body) for 2 hours in a locked S3 bucket for debugging? Need to validate prompt shaping and tokenization. Will not capture user creds intentionally, but want to confirm approach before I enable it.

Alex: @Jamie: need details: which headers, retention, who gets access, and scrub/hashing plan. Also, any PII in prompts (emails, phone numbers, SSNs)? :eyes:

Jamie: Good call. Plan proposal:
- Endpoint: /v1/infer/batch (prod namespace but only from a single goroutine pool, we'll route a tiny % to staging capture)
- Sampling: 100% for the failing customer only (customer-id=acct_93), otherwise 0%
- Duration: 2 hours window (one-off)
- Storage: encrypted S3 path s3://redwood-debug/ephemeral/2189004321/
- Access: IAM group infra-debugging (0.5 day TTL on role assumed), plus Security will have read logs
- Scrubbing: remove Authorization and cookie headers entirely. For prompt/body: replace token-like patterns and emails with hashed placeholders: e.g., user@example.com -> EMAIL_HASH:sha256(...). Keep prompt text otherwise so we can repro tokenization.

Taylor: A couple of clarifying Qs: 1) How are you hashing? Deterministic hash can leak membership if attacker has the original values. 2) Will we store the raw file anywhere else (ELK)?

Jamie: Hashing: HMAC-SHA256 with a per-customer ephemeral salt stored only in KMS for this job. Deterministic so we can link across events for the same customer during the window but not globally reversible. No other sinks, only the encrypted S3 path. We'll add object lifecycle rule to auto-delete after 2 hours + 30 mins buffer.

Alex: Security notes:
- Authorization header must be dropped completely (not hashed).
- For any token-like fields in body, prefer to replace with static [REDACTED_TOKEN] rather than hashed value.
- Emails and phone numbers: hashing with HMAC is OK for short window, but require unique per-run salt and logging that salt use in the audit trail.
- Ensure bucket has SSE-KMS using key redwood-debug-key and that we enable S3 access logging to a separate bucket.

Morgan: Ops: Can we reduce blast radius by limiting source IPs to the customer's IP ranges and only from one region? Also prefer sampling 1 in 10 requests if we can still reproduce — full capture is riskier.

Jamie: The bug only reproduces with full sequence of user messages; sampling misses it. But I can limit to the failing customer's CIDR and to us-east-1. Also I'll run it during low traffic hours to reduce exposure.

Alex: Ok re: approvals: I can greenlight with these conditions:
1) Authorization header removed server-side before storage.
2) Tokens replaced with [REDACTED_TOKEN].
3) Emails/phones HMAC-SHA256 with ephemeral KMS-stored salt, salt referenced in encrypted audit metadata (no plaintext salt in logs).
4) S3 lifecycle + object lock to auto-delete at last_message_ts + 2.5 hours.
5) Only members of infra-debugging and Security can assume role; assume-role TTL <= 8 hours.

Jamie: Sounds fair. I'll implement scrubbing in the proxy (pre-write hook) and post the exact config here before enabling. ETA 30m.

sec-bot: Incident capture policy check: ephemeral captures must be approved by one security lead and one product/ops owner. Recording approval: pending.

Taylor: Quick code snippet for the pre-write scrub (pseudo):
```
let clean = req.body.replace(/Authorization:.*\n/, '');
clean = clean.replace(/(\b\w+@\w+\.\w+\b)/g, (m) => hmac_sha256(m, run_salt));
clean = clean.replace(/(Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9\-\._~\+\/]+=*)/g, '[REDACTED_TOKEN]');
// upload clean to encrypted bucket with metadata {run_id, customer_id, salt_ref}
```

Alex: That looks fine as long as the Authorization regex runs on headers and the token regex covers all known patterns. Also add a validation step to ensure no Authorization string remains before the S3 PUT.

Morgan: I'll prepare the infra role and bucket policy. Once Jamie posts the final scrub config I'll attach the IAM ARN and link to the KMS grant.

Jamie: Posting final scrub config now (will enable 30m after Morgan confirms infra):
- Headers: drop Authorization, Cookie, X-Internal-Auth
- Body: replace Bearer, any 32+ char hex token patterns -> [REDACTED_TOKEN]
- Emails/phones: HMAC-SHA256 with kms:/keys/redwood-ephemeral, salt stored as encrypted metadata
- Storage: s3://redwood-debug/ephemeral/2189004321/ with SSE-KMS redwood-debug-key, access logging to s3://redwood-audit-logs/
- Retention: auto-delete after 2.5 hours

Alex: Approved by me (Alex). Please capture only the failing customer's traffic and notify customer success that we're doing a short debug window. Post a brief summary here when complete and confirm deletion. :white_check_mark:

Jamie: Thanks all — enabling in 25m. Will report back with deletion confirmation.

Morgan: IAM role ARN: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/infra-debugging (assume-role TTL 4h). KMS grant created. S3 bucket policy applied. Ready to flip.

Jamie: Enabled capture. Will stop at 2189007822.

Jamie: Capture complete. Files were deleted at 2189008000 as scheduled. Confirmed no Authorization leaked. Closing this thread.
